utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case Number IT-03-69-PT, The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Will both parties make their appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Dermot Groome and with me is case manager Skye Winner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Defence in the case of Mr. Stanisic, Mr. Knoops, attorney-at-law in Amsterdam.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm Zoran Jovanovic, attorney-at-law from Belgrade defending Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Knoops and Mr. Jovanovic. Before we begin, first of all, I'd like to wish everyone here a very Happy New Year. This is the second Status Conference in this case. And prior to this Status Conference, there have been two Rule 65 ter conferences convened by Ms. Yvonne Featherstone, the Senior Legal Officer of this Chamber. And she has been informing me of the substantive content of those conferences. And let me deal -- start by dealing with a couple of outstanding motions. Since the last Status Conference, the Chamber issued a decision on 14th of November on the parties' preliminary motions on the form of indictment. In that decision, the Chamber ordered the Prosecution to submit an amended indictment to which the Prosecution complied on 9th of December of last year. While the Trial Chamber has not yet issued a decision on the submitted amended indictment, both of the Defence teams filed a motion concerning an alleged defect in the amended indictment. And the Prosecution has filed a joint response to these motions. And the Chamber will render its decision in due course. And for the next matter concerning a confidential filing, shall we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to the issue of disclosure. I understand that Rule 66(A)(i) disclosure is complete, but Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosures are still outstanding. Can I hear the status of that from Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. Rule 66(A)(i) is complete, and we are in the process and plan to imminently commence the process of meeting our disclosure obligations under both 66(A)(ii) and 68, and Rule 68. If I may, if it pleases the Court, I would explain the proposal of the schedule that the Prosecution -- the schedule that the Prosecution would propose for completion of that disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Court may or may not know, since the last Status Conference the Prosecution has -- the Prosecution team on the Stanisic case has lost four professional staff and two legal interns. So we are in the process of reconstituting the team. I expect in the near future we will have a full complement of attorneys and other necessary staff, but it has caused some problems in getting off to a start with our disclosure obligations. What the Prosecution is proposing, Your Honour, is that commencing in February we begin disclosure both of Rule 66(A)(ii) and Rule 68, and for every month thereafter continue to make a disclosure once a month of both Rules 66(A)(ii) and Rule 68. We estimate that proceeding in that way, we would be able to complete all of the disclosure under Rule 68 and Rule 66(A)(ii) --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My apologies. That we would be able to complete all of the disclosure for both 66 and 68 by July, before the summer break. Prosecution also has a proposal with respect to the mechanics of some of this disclosure. I don't know if the Chamber would like me to address that now or to address it separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you mean by mechanics? Yes, if you can address that matter now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Wherever possible, Your Honour, we will be disclosing electronically. We will be providing compact disks with search engines so the Defence may search whatever is disclosed to them. In a case of material that is available either in the disclosure suite or on the ICTY website -- for example, open session testimony of witnesses in other proceedings -- what the Prosecution would propose to do is the following: To meet our disclosure obligation by identifying the relevant testimony or the relevant document to the Defence and allowing them to download that material at their convenience directly from the source. So it's a matter -- it's our position that there would be no tangible difference between downloading it from a CD or downloading it from the website. Of course, we'll be guided by the Chamber's views on this. But proceeding in that way would permit us to expedite the disclosure process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As long as they consent to that method of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will discuss it then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's set aside the Rule 68 disclosure a moment, and let's concentrate on 66(A)(ii) disclosure. Is there any observation from the Defence team on the -- regarding the method of disclosure Mr. Groome just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Stanisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank You, Your Honour. We had discussed this issue with at the 65 ter meeting so I suppose you are familiar with the result. As for the disclosure method suggested by Mr. Groome, we do, indeed, have access to this website of the Tribunal, and the Defence does not need to be advised specially of which witnesses these are. However, I believe that the transcripts available on the site of the Tribunal are not sufficient in themselves. We cannot analyse the testimony of one witness without having received his witness statements in advance. I have nothing against following the website of the ICTY, but I believe it is slightly unusual for the Prosecution to not deliver everything that concerns a particular witness, and leave the Defence teams only with what is available on the website. I believe, therefore, the Prosecution should make an effort to identify the witnesses as suggested by Mr. Groome, but also disclose everything available in connection with those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise if I wasn't clear enough. Obviously 66(A)(ii), my obligations under that encompass far more than simply what's available publicly on the website. We will, of course, then, be providing electronic copies of witness statements and any other material that would be covered by Rule 66(A)(ii), without question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the list or index you're proposing to disclose is -- will work as a kind of search tool or courtesy tool for the Defence, and the full disclosure will follow. Am I correct in understanding so?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour. Perhaps if I can put it in other words. Let's say there's Witness A, and Witness A perhaps has testified in the Milosevic trial. What we will be providing to Defence counsel as soon as we are able is a list that says "Witness A testified on this date and his testimony is publicly available." And then as soon as we are able, we will be providing Witness A's statement and any other disclosable material in electric form which is not readily available from the website.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there any objection from the Defence in receiving the statement in electronic form?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, none whatsoever as far as the form of disclosure is concerned, whether electronic or otherwise. The only thing that matters to the Defence is that we cannot do with the transcripts available only on the website. It is something for the public domain, but that is not sufficient for preparing our case. Of course, we have nothing against receiving documents in electronic form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding is that is exactly what the Prosecution plans to do. And let's call it the offering the list or index of first disclosure, when do you think the first disclosure can be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Proposing to begin in February, Your Honour, and then continuing every month thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In all, it will be complete by the end of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could just add the following observation: One of the reasons why I decided upon this is it allows us to commence disclosure as soon as possible given the circumstances that we face, and ensures that the Defence receives a steady stream of documents rather than receiving an overwhelming number on a date determined by the Chamber, but that they receive a steady stream of documents so they can work in preparing their Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And there must be some sensitive statements or security-concerned statements the Prosecution is seeking for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. And the Prosecution would ask or would plan, again, trying to balance -- is planning, my apologies, is planning to file a protective measures' motion that would encompass nearly all of the witnesses or all of the witnesses that we presently know about and intend to call by the middle of April. And we are calculating that from the time that we believe our obligations in the Milosevic have receded a bit and gives us about four weeks to make our final contacts with the witnesses and to put together a comprehensive application for protective measures. That, also, Your Honour, I believe would give -- taking into account the time the Chamber would need to decide that motion, would still allow us to complete the disclosure, according to what I've proposed, on schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the Registrar has the calendar with her right now? Or... I note the 20th of July is -- I'm sorry. 19th of July is Monday. So Mr. Groome, what do you think about my ordering that 19th of July is the deadline for 66(A)(ii) disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution is grateful for that amount of time, and we'll do our best to comply with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's think about the -- I understand there's an

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned friend Mr. Jovanovic had asked that we deal with this matter in private session. I don't know if Mr. Jovanovic wants to be heard on it first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you think you can complete this disclosure earlier than the 66(A)(ii) disclosure, or you're suggesting to complete this at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm suggesting that it be put on the same schedule, Your Honour, but I have a query that I would put to my colleagues that may help us expedite this process. We've provided the Defence with search terms that we believe will assist us in locating and identifying Rule 68 material in our collection. Many of those search terms are the same search terms that were used in the Milosevic case. If the Defence agrees to accept the results of those search terms without a separate review, the disclosure of Rule 68 material can begin sooner. The difference in what they will receive is that they perhaps may receive a few additional documents. There is material that may be Rule 68 in the Milosevic case that would not be Rule 68 material in this particular case. I cannot imagine a situation where the reverse of that is true. So if the Defence are willing to accept the results of our search terms for the Milosevic case, we can begin almost immediately to turn over a large portion of that Rule 68 material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would very much encourage the cooperation in that matter from the Defence. But is there any comment from the Defence on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you for this opportunity to remark. At this moment, the Defence has no additional search terms provided to the Prosecution. We cannot exclude, of course, that these terms could emerge during the disclosure process. So we have to reserve our right to file additional search terms. We did file, the Defence for Mr. Stanisic, did file a preliminary list with agreed and disputed facts. Therefore, they could potentially enhire [sic] several search terms. But at this stage, we have no additional remarks for the search list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then, the same date will be ordered as the deadline for the exculpatory material. And then I'd like to hear any comments, report on expert reports in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just prior to the proceedings beginning today, the Prosecution turned over the materials with respect to three of the experts. We are in the process of completing the work with the experts, the other experts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How many in all? I'm sorry to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We anticipate five experts all together, Your Honour. So that would leave two. Not only have we provided today the expert reports, but we've provided CDs with all of the underlying documents that were relied on by some of the experts. I'm sorry, one of the experts. All of the underlying that that expert relied upon. It's our intention to disclose the others as soon as they come available. I'm unable at this time to give the Court a definitive date as to when the other two reports will be completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can it be safe if I order the same date for the deadline of the expert also?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I dealt with most of the important issues related to the disclosure. Are there any matters the parties wish to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: There's one additional matter, Your Honour, the Defence wants to point to, and I think it belongs to the confidentiality of the provisional release motion, so I would respectfully request to go to private --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just a brief comment with respect to disclosure pursuant to Rule 68. I consider that something that can be brought under Rule 68 in this case does not automatically mean that it can come under the same rule in a different case, in the Milosevic case, for example. So I don't think any automation ought to be applied. It oughtn't to be automatic. I understand the importance in the Milosevic case, of course, and the Prosecution's attitude towards it, the database that can be used for other trials as well, such as witness statements and other exhibits and evidence with respect to the circumstances and facts. But I just simply believe that we can't apply the criteria automatically, those that hold true in the Milosevic case and this case, too. One must take all the elements into consideration. And just one more point with respect to the problem that I -- a problem I encountered, and I brought this up at a meeting we had. The Trial Chamber and you, Your Honour, are a member of that Trial Chamber made a ruling that I be allowed access to transcripts and evidence from the Milosevic trial. However, after that ruling, I approached the registry in November and again in December, and called them up several times on the phone asking them for a list of exhibits and witnesses that were produced during the Milosevic trial and which related to Bosnia and Croatia. I have received no response to the present day. So you gave me access. You allowed me to have insight into them, whereas the registry simply does not wish to inform me what witnesses were heard during the Milosevic trial and which exhibits were tendered. So let me repeat: I consider that I cannot rely on the website of the Tribunal alone or the televised trial of the Milosevic case in order to gain access to things that are relevant to me. So quite simply, I would ask the registry to allow me to have access to that matter. I have made the same motion with respect to the Samac case. The Prosecution has not yet responded. I am awaiting their response. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I will look into the second matter. And the first issue will be noted by the Prosecution. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt the Chamber, I just want to make an observation regarding the Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Of course our Rule 68 obligation is unique to this case, and we undertake it with full vigour. What I'm simply speaking about are those search terms which are identical. And perhaps it will help Mr. Jovanovic if I give a concrete example. One of the terms that was searched, was, let's say, Red Berets for the Milosevic case, and all the documents that had that word in it were then read by trained people to identify any material that was exculpatory, or Rule 68, for the Milosevic case. That would include any material that because of the legal theory of that case that would have exculpated either Mr. Stanisic or Mr. Simatovic. So what I have proposed is that if Mr. Jovanovic will accept those documents that are now ready to be given, we are willing to do that almost immediately. If Mr. Jovanovic would prefer that we go through those documents again and pull out those documents that are only exculpatory to Mr. Milosevic and not to his client, then that will take a considerable amount of time and will slow down the process. That is all I'm suggesting when I made that proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then the last issue will be the next Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Would you allow me to ask my client if he has other issues to be made before you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: -- close the session with a next date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you for your time. And sorry for the interruption. Mr. Stanisic has no additional comments and questions to the Chamber or the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we set the date for the next Status Conference, given that the Prosecution was given sufficient time to complete its obligation for disclosure, is it possible for the Prosecution to file its pre-trial brief at the same date, which means the end of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So 19th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So it will be so ordered. Then can I ask the Defence how much time you need for the preparation of pre-trial brief on the Defence side after you receive the Prosecution's pre-trial brief? If I can -- but that can be dealt with at the next Status Conference, not right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So you don't want an answer yet right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you can, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: I think we will confer together with respect to the time, if you don't mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then the next Status Conference should be held before 19th of May this year. And I think that's the deadline. So a scheduling order will be issued when the time approaches, around 19th of May. Unless there's anything, this hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: at 4.03 p.m.
